explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The creation of the Technical Education and Skills Development Authority (TESDA) on August 25, 1994, through the merger of the former National Manpower and Youth Council (NMYC), the Bureau of Technical Vocational Education of the then Department of Education, Culture and Sports (BTVE-DECS) and the Apprenticeship program of the Department of Labor and Employment (DOLE), was an offshoot of the trifocalization of education recommended by the 1991 Congresssional Education Commission or EDCOM. By virtue of Republic Act No. 7796 (TESDA Act of 1994), the TESDA is mandated to ensure the delivery of relevant, accessible, high quality and efficient technical education and skills development and to develop high quality middle-level manpower responsive to the country’s development goals and priorities. However, after more than two decades of delivering relevant, accessible, and efficient technical education and skills development thoughout ther country, TESDA has been encountering many challenges and limitations that affect the performance of its functions, delivery of technical-vocational education and training (TVET) programs, and fulfillment of its vision. One of these is the need to sstrengthen its organizational structure and functions to keep pace with the advent of technology and the demands of the Fourth Industrial Revolution (4IR). The frequent transfer of the TESDA from one office to another has also affected its functions, programs and projects, and delivery of educational services. From an attached agency of the Department of Labor and Employment, TESDA was transferred to the Office of the President and now, to the Department of Trade and Industry through executive order signed by President Duterte. Moreover, under the TESDA Charter, the TESDA Director-General shall enjoy the benefits, privileges ad emoluments equivalent to the rank of Undersecretary. However, the current and past two Presidents of the Philippines appointed the TESDA Director General with a Cabinet rank position or equivalent to a Secretary. By elevating the TESDA into a department, it shall be headed by a Secretary, four (4) Undersecretaries and four (4) Assistant Secretaries and attain self-determination to ensure permanence and continuity of mandated programs. This will also strengthen the implementing, regulatory, and policy-making functions of the agency, as well as make it more responsive and agile in the era of the 4IR and digital economy. The proposed Department of Technical Education and Skills Development (DTESD) will not only improve the resource/budget allocation for TVET programs, but will also ably represent the TVET sector as a whole, changing its “second class” perception. More importantly, the proposed DTESD will have a better capacity to fulfill its vision as the transformational leader in TVET in the country. The immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The 1987 Constitution of the Philippines Article XII, Section 14 provides that "The sustained development of a reservoir of national talents consisting of Filipino scientists, entrepreneurs, professionals, managers, high-level technical manpower and skilled workers and craftsmen in all fields shall be promoted by the State." The Constitution likewise asserts in Article XIV, Section 1 that "The State shall protect and promote the right of all citizens to quality education at all levels and shall take appropriate steps to make such education accessible to all." Also, Article XIV, Section 2 emphasizes the govemment's duty to ensure a complete and suitable education system that meets the needs of the people in an ever-changing environment. It also calls for support for students through scholarships and other aid, especially for those from underprivileged backgrounds. Additionally, it promotes alternative leaming approaches, including informal and community-based programs. Critical to the promotion of sustained development of a highly skilled work force, the Technical Education and Skills Development Authority (TESDA) was established through Republic Act No. 7796 (TESDA Act of 1994) on August 25,1994. Through the merging of National Manpower and Youth Council (NMYC), Bureau of Technical and Vocational Education (BTVE), and the Apprenticeship Program of the Bureau of Local Employment a3LE), TESDA is mandated to oversee skills development, set standards, accredit institutions, fund projects, and support trainer programs for the development of a top-quality middle-level manpower capable of adapting towards emerging issues and necessities of the Fourth Industrial Revolution. TESDA has aimed to set the direction, promulgate relevant standards, and implement programs geared towards a quality-assured and inclusive technical education and skills development and certification system for the country's technical-vocational education and training (TVET) system. The frequent transfer between various administrative entities has been driven by different factors, including changes in government priorities, administrative restructuring, and attempts to enhance coordination between TESDA and other government agencies. However, these transfers have often resulted in disruptions to TESDA's operations, delays in the implementation of programs, and challenges in maintaining continuity and coherence in policy and programmatic efforts. Recognizing the need for stability, coherence, and focused leadership in the promotion of technical education and skills development, this bill proposes the establishment of the Department of Technical Education and Skills Development (DTESD) as a permanent and dedicated government agency. By elevating TESDA into a department, the bill aims to provide TESDA with the necessary institutional franiework, authority, and resources to effectively cany out its mandate in a sustained and coherent manner. The creation of the DTESD is envisioned to address the ever-changing labor landscape and its frequent transfers between different government offices. By consolidating efforts in TVET development under a single department, the bill seeks to streamline governance, enhance coordination, and ensure the continuity and effectiveness of policies and programs aimed at developing a skilled and globally competitive workforce in the Philippines. Approval of this bill is earnestly sought. REP. II); the State shall give priority to education, science and technology, arts, culture, and sports to foster patriotism and nationalism, accelerate social progress, and promote total human liberation and development (Sec. 17, Art. The State shall give priority to research and development, invention, innovation, and their utilization; and to science and technology education, training, and services. It shall support indigenous, appropriate, and self-reliant scientific and technological capabilities, and their application to the country’s productive systems and national life (Sec. 10, Art. XIV). In this regard, the Technical Education and Skills Development Authority (TESDA) which was created by virtue of Republic Act 7796, otherwise known as the “Technical Education and Skills Development Act of 1994” is the government agency tasked to manage and supervise technical education and skills development in the Philippines. TESDA’s vision is a transformational leader in the technical education and skills development of the Filipino workforce, with a mission of setting directions, promulgating relevant standards, and implementing programs geared towards a quality-assured and inclusive technical education and skills development and certification system. Under the bill, the proposed Department of Technical Education and Skills Development (DTESD) shall be the primary policy formulation, planning, coordinating, implementing, regulatory, and administrative entity of the government for technical education and training programs. With its gargantuan task, it is believed that by converting Page 1 of 15 it into a Department, TESDA will be strengthened as an implementing and regulatory institution of the technical and vocational sector. It will make this Agency in a better position to fulfill its vision and mission, believing in demonstrated competence, institutional integrity, personal commitment, culture of innovativeness, and a deep sense of nationalism. explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Technical Education and Skills Development Authority (TESDA) was established through the enactment of Republic Act No. 7796 otherwise known as the "Technical Education and Skills Development Act of 1994" with the aim to encourage the full participation of and mobilize the industry, labor, local government units and technical vocational institutions in the skills development of the country's human resources. The said Act integrated the functions of the former National Manpower and Youth Council (NMYC), the Bureau of Technical- Vocational Education of the Department of Education, Culture and Sports (BTVE-DECS) and the Office of Apprenticeship of the Department of Labor and Employment (DOLE) as a result of a national review of the state of Philippine education and manpower development which was undertaken by the Congressional Commission on Education back in 1991. TESDA has been the leading authority managing technical skills education in the Philippines. Its major thrust is the formulation of a comprehensive development plan for middle-level manpower based on the National Technical Education and Skills Development Plan that includes apprenticeship, dual training system and other similar schemes. TESDA is also improving its language course offerings in partnership with foreign embassies and international organizations consistent with the strategy to reposition technical vocational education and training (TVET) for global competitiveness. The language-related courses —Arabic, Mandarin, Korean, Italian and French —will be added to the existing courses under its National Skills Language Center (NLSC). In 2018 alone, there are more than 2 million who benefitted in the agency’s various Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) program. For twenty-five (25) years, after the passage of Republic Act No. 7796 or the TESDA Act which was enacted on August 25, 1994, continues to be in the forefront in ensuring that Filipinos have access to technical education and skills development (TESD) that is not only relevant and efficient, but also accessible and of high quality. Despite much progress and lives changed, the agency is facing various and enormous challenges in order to adapt to the ever- changing local and global environment that the organization needs to focus on. In order to meet world standards, TESDA must address the need for modern facilities and equipment to level with the requirements in addressing the challenges created by the 4IR (Fourth Industrial Revolution) and other advancements that may happen in the future. It must also be bestowed with the police powers to impose sanctions and penalties to erring TESD implementers. These are among the limitations to what TESDA can do which can be ultimately addressed if the agency will be elevated into a line Department of the government. This proposed Bill seeks to repeal R.A. 7796 or the TESDA Act of 1994 and to reinforce the powers and organizational function of TESDA by turning it into a Department. The proposed Department shall become the primary policy formulation, planning, coordinating, implementing, regulating and administrative entity of the government for technical education and training and certification policies, plans, and programs. It shall be headed by a Secretary, four (4) Undersecretaries and four (4) Assistant Secretaries. Page | 1 With the proposed legislative measure, TESDA will be strengthened as an implementing and regulatory institution of the Technical and Vocational Sector of the country’s trifocal education system. This measure is made in the interest of the Filipinos who wants to regain new skills and improve their well-being, and will be achieved in greater capacity vision as the transformational leader in the technical education and skills development of the Filipino workforce. The immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Technical Education and Skills Development Authority (TESDA) was established on August 25, 1994, by virtue of Republic Act No. 7796, otherwise known as the “Technical Education and Skills Development Act of 1994.” Since its creation, TESDA has remained an essential contributor to the National Government’s mission of providing Filipinos with quality-assured technical education and skills development programs, and mobilizing technical-vocational institutions across the country. Over three decades after its establishment, TESDA continues to serve as the leading government agency responsible for setting the direction of, and ensuring the efficient delivery of, technical education and skills development programs across various sectors nationwide. However, TESDA has also faced challenges and limitations, particularly in today’s ever-changing local and global environment. To address pressing concerns such as strengthening TESDA’s organizational structure and modernizing skills training facilities, the overall system of the Authority must be enhanced through an increased budget, as well as sufficient personnel and resources. Hence, this proposed measure seeks to repeal Republic Act No. 7796, or the “Technical Education and Skills Development Act of 1994,” and strengthen the powers and organizational functions of TESDA by transforming it into a full-fledged Department. The Department shall serve as the primary policy- making, planning, coordinating, implementing, regulating, and administrative entity of the government for technical education, training, and certification programs. It shall be headed by a Secretary, supported by four (4) Undersecretaries and four (4) Assistant Secretaries. Such a reform is necessary to address challenges and implement policies consistent with the demands of the Fourth Industrial Revolution and other global advancements. Through this proposed legislative measure, TESDA will be further strengthened as the implementing and regulatory institution for the Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) sector within the country’s trifocal education system. Most importantly, this measure is being filed to promote the interests and meet the needs of the hardworking and highly skilled Filipino workforce. In view of the foregoing, the approval of this bill is earnestly sought. JONATHA) T. explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The creation of the Technical Education and Skills Development Authority (TESDA) on August 25, 1994, through the merger of the former National Manpower and Youth Council (NMYC), the Bureau of Technical Vocational Education of the then Department of Education, Culture and Sports (BTVE-DECS) and the Apprenticeship program of the Department of Labor and Employment (DOLE), was an offshoot of the trifocalization of education recommended by the 1991 Congresssional Education Commission or EDCOM. By virtue of Republic Act No. 7796 (TESDA Act of 1994), the TESDA is mandated to ensure the delivery of relevant, accessible, high quality and efficient technical education and skills development and to develop high quality middle-level manpower responsive to the country’s development goals and priorities. However, after more than two decades of delivering relevant, accessible, and efficient technical education and skills development thoughout ther country, TESDA has been encountering many challenges and limitations that affect the performance of its functions, delivery of technical-vocational education and training (TVET) programs, and fulfillment of its vision. One of these is the need to sstrengthen its organizational structure and functions to keep pace with the advent of technology and the demands of the Fourth Industrial Revolution (4IR). The frequent transfer of the TESDA from one office to another has also affected its functions, programs and projects, and delivery of educational services. From an attached agency of the Department of Labor and Employment, TESDA was transferred to the Office of the President and now, to the Department of Trade and Industry through executive order signed by President Duterte. Moreover, under the TESDA Charter, the TESDA Director-General shall enjoy the benefits, privileges ad emoluments equivalent to the rank of Undersecretary. However, the current and past two Presidents of the Philippines appointed the TESDA Director General with a Cabinet rank position or equivalent to a Secretary. By elevating the TESDA into a department, it shall be headed by a Secretary, four (4) Undersecretaries and four (4) Assistant Secretaries and attain self-determination to ensure permanence and continuity of mandated programs. This will also strengthen the implementing, regulatory, and policy-making functions of the agency, as well as make it more responsive and agile in the era of the 4IR and digital economy. The proposed Department of Technical Education and Skills Development (DTESD) will not only improve the resource/budget allocation for TVET programs, but will also ably represent the TVET sector as a whole, changing its “second class” perception. More importantly, the proposed DTESD will have a better capacity to fulfill its vision as the transformational leader in TVET in the country. The immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. title: AN ACT CREATING THE DEPARTMENT OF TECHNICAL EDUCATION, TRAINING AND CERTIFICATION, DEFINING ITS POWERS AND FUNCTIONS, AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7796, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “TESDA ACT OF 1994”, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Philippines, with its growing economy, faces a significant challenge in bridging the skills gap in its workforce. Technical-vocational education and training (TVET) play a crucial role in developing a skilled labor force capable of meeting the demands of modern industries. However, the country has long faced inefficiencies in the management and delivery of TVET programs. These challenges stem from fragmented governance, outdated curricula, underfunding, and mismatched industry needs, among others. The Philippine technical education system is divided among various government agencies, which results in inconsistent policies, misallocation of resources, and lack of coordination. TESDA oversees skills development, while DepEd handles secondary-level vocational programs. Higher education institutions (HEIs) also offer technical courses under the Commission on Higher Education (CHED). This fragmented structure complicates the implementation of nationwide reforms and makes it difficult to monitor and evaluate the quality of training programs. Likewise, the skills taught in many TVET programs do not always meet the evolving demands of industries. While TESDA has attempted to bridge this gap, there is still a lag in updating curricula and aligning programs with technological advancements and market needs. Many TVET institutions lack modern equipment, and instructors often receive inadequate training. These deficiencies hinder the development of a skilled workforce capable of competing in global markets. There are geographic and socioeconomic barriers that limit access to quality technical education. Many regions, particularly in rural areas, lack sufficient training centers and resources to support the growing demand for skilled workers. The establishment of a Department of Technical Education and Training (DTET) will centralize the management of technical education and training across various levels. This new department will be tasked with the integration of TVET programs under one cohesive strategy, improving coordination among government agencies, educational institutions, and industries. The DTET will streamline decision-making processes, ensuring that policies and programs are coordinated and aligned with national economic priorities. This unified governance will help resolve issues of duplication and inefficiency, leading to a more coherent and effective TVET system. The DTET will be empowered to work closely with industries and employers to identify current and future skill requirements. By fostering partnerships with private sector organizations, the DTET can ensure that TVET curricula are continuously updated to meet the demands of emerging industries such as digital technologies, renewable energy, and healthcare. Studies, such as those by the Asian Development Bank (ADB), have stressed the need for curricula reforms that align education with labor market needs to reduce the skills mismatch. The creation of a dedicated department will allow for better prioritization and allocation of resources toward upgrading infrastructure, purchasing modern equipment, and improving the professional development of trainers and instructors. This will ensure that TVET institutions are equipped to deliver high-quality education. Additionally, the DTET can advocate for more sustainable and long-term funding for technical education programs, ensuring their continuity and expansion. With a single department overseeing all aspects of TVET, the DTET will be able to implement nationwide strategies to expand access to training, especially in underserved regions. Through initiatives like mobile training units, partnerships with local government units (LGUs), and the expansion of online and blended learning, the DTET can ensure that technical education opportunities are available to all Filipinos, regardless of their geographic or socioeconomic background. The creation of the Department of Technical Education and Training in the Philippines is a vital step toward improving the country’s technical education system. By centralizing governance, aligning curricula with industry needs, improving resource allocation, and expanding access, the DTET will help produce a highly skilled and employable workforce capable of driving economic growth and meeting the demands of an evolving labor market. Through this proposed legislation, the Philippines can build a robust technical education system that supports both individual and national development. In view of the foregoing, immediate approval of this bill is earnestly sought. DALE B. title: AN ACT CREATING THE DEPARTMENT OF TECHNICAL EDUCATION AND SKILLS DEVELOPMENT, DEFINING ITS POWERS AND FUNCTIONS, REPEALING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7796, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE TESDA ACT OF 1994 AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE In an increasingly competitive and rapidly evolving global economy, the country must ensure that its workforce possesses relevant, high-quality, and industry-responsive skills. While existing systems under the Republic Act No. 7796 created the Technical Education and Skills Development Authority (TESDA), there is a growing need to elevate and strengthen this mandate into a full-fledged department to better address persistent issues such as job mismatch, unemployment, underemployment, and unequal access to skills training. Thus, this bill measure seeks to establish the Department of Technical Education and Skills Development (DTESD) as the primary government body responsible for the formulation, coordination, implementation, and regulation of policies and programs on technical education and skills development (TESD) in the Philippines. 1 The DTESD will be mandated to formulate a National Technical Education and Skills Development Plan (NTESDP) to guide the country’s manpower development strategy and ensure alignment with national development goals. Further, it will prioritize access to technical education for marginalized and disadvantaged sectors, including beneficiaries of the Pantawid Pamilyang Pilipino Program (4Ps) under Republic Act No. 11310, to support poverty reduction and inclusive growth. By transforming TESDA into a full department, we can expect improvement in the quality and global competitiveness of Filipino workers, reduction in job-skills mismatch, expansion of employment and livelihood opportunities, strengthening of industry participation in workforce development and enhancement of social mobility. Finally, we recognize Rep. Mark O. Go of the Lone District of Baguio for filing a similar bill in the Nineteenth Congresses. In view of the foregoing, the passage of this bill is earnestly sought. title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE DEPARTMENT OF CULTURE, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The culture and the arts are not just mere forms of expression and entertainment, more importantly, they are essential tools for nation-building. Arts and Culture are integral to a nation’s struggle for national identity as they can evoke dialogue, induce reflection, and charter new relationships and ideas—all of which are essential to a healthy society. This is exemplified through the works of renowned Filipino artists during the Spanish and American Colonial Period, which have helped shape a sense of national identity among Filipinos. It is the policy of the State under Section 17, Article II of the Constitution to give priority to arts and culture so as to “foster patriotism nationalism, accelerate social progress, and promote total human liberation and development.” However, with the transfer of the administration of cultural agencies to the National Commission on Culture Arts from the then Department of Education, Culture and Sports, effective promotion of the culture and arts took the sidelines due to the limited powers and resources of the NCCA and attached agencies. To this end, this proposed measure seeks to reorganize the National Commission on Culture and Arts into an independent Department of Culture or Kagawaran ng Kultura which shall be the primary policy- formulating, planning, coordinating, implementing, and administrative entity of the executive branch of the National Government that will develop, manage and implement the pertinent provisions of the Constitution regarding culture and arts. With more powers and better resources, the creation of the Department of Culture would be better equipped for the enormous task of preservation of the Filipino heritage and the promotion and advancement of cultural education among Filipinos. On behalf of the people of Parañaque City’s Second District, and for the common good of the Filipino people, the approval of the said measure is earnestly sought. REP. GUSTAVO S. explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Culture, which is the broad spectrum of people's beliefs, practices, customs and traditions, and other forms of actual and symbolic expressions which are handed from generation to generation, plays a big role in creating the country's national identity, despite of its diversity. It brings together Filipinos although separated by different islands, beliefs and customs. It is what binds the Filipinos as one. Thus, in order to further develop Philippine culture to reach heights in advancing the Philippines' national identity, the creation of a Department of Culture is hereby proposed. The Department of Culture shall, among others, focus on the protection, preservation, regulation, development, management, dissemination and promotion of the cultural, historical and artistic heritage and resources, tangible and intangible, of the Philippines and the Filipino people. As such, the passage of this Bill is earnestly sought. EDWIN L. explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Filipino culture is rich and diverse. It is a reflection of the people's faith and a culmination of their stories and values. At its core, the concepts of "pakikipagkapzm tao/' the celebration of life, and oneness with nature have shaped our way of life for centuries. Deeply rooted in history and tradition, the State recognizes culture to have a significant role in our society as it defines our identity and unifies all Filipinos. Thus, the Constitution mandates the State to prioritize arts and culture, and to foster the preservation, enrichment, and dynamic evolution of Filipino culture to promote nationalism and human development and boost social and economic progress. Despite the positive impact of culture on our country and its people, culture is often ignored as a central factor in socio-economic progress and in enhancing the quality of life. For one, it is an empowering tool for local and indigenous groups and provides people with opportunities to come together. It is also environmentally conscientious to preserve older structures, which in turn attracts tourism, brings investments to communities, and many more. The importance and prioritization given to it over the past decades are not commensurate with its extent and value. Now, more than ever, the protection and management of our culture are necessary to ensure that its values and functions are maximized for the benefit of all generations - past, present, and future. Recognizing the role played by the National Commission for Culture and the Arts (NCCA) in implementing the cultural programs of the government and the importance of the culture and the arts in the enricliment of the Filipino identity despite the limited resources, such importance must be echoed in appropriate and improved government structures and increased funding. Therefore, this bill seeks to reorganize the existing NCCA into the Department of Culture, safeguarding its place in the priorities of the government and ensuring that the finest elements of our culture will be passed on for generations to come. explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Culture is a key driver of inclusive development, soft power, innovation, and national identity. Deeply rooted in history and tradition, it shapes who we are as a people and unites Filipinos across regions and generations. The 1987 Constitution affirms this by mandating the State to prioritize arts and culture to foster patriotism and nationalism, accelerate social progress, and promote total human liberation and development. Culture empowers local and Indigenous communities, fosters participation and solidarity, and contributes to human development, community cohesion, and socio­ economic transformation. It also offers sustainable pathways for development through the conservation of heritage structures, the promotion of cultural tourism, and the revitalization of local economies. Yet despite this vast potential, the Philippines has yet to establish a dedicated Department of Culture, unlike many of its neighbors in Southeast and East Asia. This institutional gap has led to fragmented policy direction, chronic underinvestment, and missed opportunities to fully harness our rich cultural assets. While the National Commission for Culture and the Arts (NCCA) serves as the primary coordinating and policy-making body, it is not a line agency and lacks direct authority over many of the cultural institutions responsible for implementation. As a result, the cultural sector remains underprioritized in national development planning and falls short of its potential as a strategic pillar of growth and national unity. According to UNESCO, cultural and creative industries generate nearly US$2.3 trillion in annual global revenues, equivalent to 3.1 percent of the world's gross domestic product (GDP). Their contribution to national value added varies among G20 economies, ranging from 0.7 percent in Mexico to 3 percent in the United States. These industries also provide employment for approximately 6.2 percent of the global workforce.1 In the Asia-Pacific region, countries like Japan and South Korea have successfully institutionalized cultural governance, generating massive returns. In 2023, Japan's anime industry (including television and film productions, streaming distribution, merchandising, music, events, and overseas licensing), supported by Agency for Cultural Affairs (Bunkachd) under the Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology (MEXT), reached an all-time high of ¥3.3465 trillion (approximately US$22.3 billion). Of the total revenue, ¥1.6243 trillion (around US$10.8 billion) came from domestic sources, while ¥1.7222 trillion (about US$11.5 billion) was generated from international markets.2 South Korea's cultural content industry (Korean Wave or Hallyu), supported by its Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism, has steadily grown into a high value-added sector marked by robust domestic sales and expanding exports. South Korea's cultural content industry grew steadily from 2021 to 2023, with total sales rising from W137.5 trillion (US$105.8 billion)3 to W154.2 trillion (US$110.5 billion),4 and exports increasing from US$12.45 billion to US$13.3 billion during the same period. 1 UN Trade and Development (UNCTAD). Retrieved July 31,2025, from https://japantoday.com/category/features/lifestyle/anime-industry-report-shows-overseas-anime- market-is-bigger-than-japanese-one-but-is-this-a-cultural-tipping-point-2 3 Invest KOREA, (n.d.). Cultural Content Invest KOREA. Retrieved August 1,2025, from https://www.investkorea.org/ik-en/cntnts/i-326/web.do 4 Son, J.-h. (2025, April 18). Policy Watch: Lee Jae-myung to double Korean culture industry revenue, exports in 7 years. The Korea Herald. Retrieved August 1,2025, from https://www.koreaherald.com/article/10468573 In contrast, the Philippines' creative economy reached PhPl.94 trillion (USD 34,64 billion) in 2024. This marked an 8.7 percent increase from the PhPl.78 trillion (USD 31.95 billion) recorded in 2023, reflecting continued expansion across key creative sectors such as digital media, advertising, symbolic content, and traditional cultural expressions,5 These data points underscore a vital truth: countries that invest in strong cultural governance and infrastructure reap significant returns, not only in terms of economic growth, employment, and exports, but also in global influence, innovation, and national unity. In contrast, the Philippines continues to operate without a dedicated Department of Culture, limiting its ability to fully harness the value of its diverse cultural assets. With the Philippines'creative economy already contributing 7.3 percent to Gross Domestic Product (GDP) and growing, the absence of a dedicated department risks leaving our rich cultural capital under-leveraged and fragmented. This bill seeks to address that institutional gap. By establishing the Department of Culture, it provides the policy leadership, operational mandate, and organizational structure necessary to protect, develop, and promote Philippine culture, both as a heritage to be preserved and as a resource to be activated for inclusive growth. Among its key features are the following: 1. Centralized cultural governance through the integration of policy, regulatory, and programmatic functions currently dispersed across multiple agencies; 2. Nationwide and international reach via regional offices and Sentro /?/za/centers to bring cultural development closer to communities and diaspora networks; 3. Capacity-building and education through national institutes dedicated to living traditions, heritage

title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A NATIONAL COMPREHENSIVE SCHOOL SAFETY PROGRAM, STRENGTHENING DISASTER RISK REDUCTION AND EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS, AND PREVENTING SCHOOL VIOLENCE, ACTIVE ASSAILANT INCIDENTS, AND OTHER SAFETY AND SECURITY THREATS, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Schools must always remain places of learning, formation, and safety. Recent successive incidents and threats involving bullying and cyberbullying, bomb scares, deadly weapons, online threats, and other acts of violence have haunted our places of learning and peace. They have also exposed the evolving risks faced by learners, teachers, and school personnel. In response, the Department of Education has strengthened its policies on weapons and bomb threats and introduced school safety audits, active-threat preparedness exercises, confidential reporting mechanisms, and mental-health interventions. Existing laws address particular aspects of school safety, including bullying, mental health, and disaster risk reduction. Nevertheless, there remains a need for a unified and permanent framework covering the prevention, preparedness, response, and recovery measures necessary to address both natural hazards and intentional acts of violence across educational institutions. This bill therefore establishes a National Comprehensive School Safety Program. It mandates school-specific safety and vulnerability assessments, emergency plans and drills, reasonable security infrastructure, weapons-control measures, violence-prevention and mental-health programs, confidential reporting and threat assessment mechanisms, inter-agency coordination, and post-incident recovery and continuity-of-learning measures. 1 Through this measure, school safety shall no longer depend on isolated or reactive interventions but shall become a coordinated, preventive, and adequately supported national responsibility. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. HON. BERNADETTE “DETTE” G. explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The worsening housing gap in lower- and middle-income countries is largely attributed to rapid urbanization and population growth outpacing the housing supply (Lee and Singh, 2022). In 2018, the Philippine housing backlog reached 5.7 million units and absent any significant intervention, this housing backlog is projected to reach 22 million by 2040 (Padojinog and Yap, 2020). Furthermore, with 4.1 million individuals displaced due to government infrastructure projects in 2019 alone (Bermudez et al., 2020) and an estimated 3.7 million Informal Settler Families (ISFs) residing in hazard-prone areas (UN-Habitat, 2023), addressing the housing backlog remains a priority concern of the government. Despite ongoing government housing initiatives targeting the housing deficit, beneficiaries of socialized housing moved in to housing units without basic services such as electricity (Ebdane, 2024). Compounding this issue, plant outages and rising consumer electricity demand consistently triggered yellow and red alerts in the transmission grid, resulting in power interruptions and prompting several legislative inquiries (Baligad, 2024). While socialized housing programs are addressing the need for shelter, many resettlement communities remain unserved or underserved in terms of reliable, affordable, and sustainable energy access. The Philippines' reliance on imported fuel makes the country highly vulnerable to external energy shocks, contributing to rising food and energy costs (De Leon, 2026). Estimated electricity rates in the country are among the highest in Asia, ranking fourth overall (Dela Peña, 2026). These conditions expose Filipino households to high energy costs, unstable power supply, or limited access to grid electricity, with greater impact to households in resettlement sites, undermining the long-term livability and sustainability of housing interventions. Coupled with the increasing frequency and intensity of climate-related hazards, the vulnerability of traditional energy systems underscores the need for resilient, decentralized, and renewable energy solutions. Article XIII, Section 9 of the 1987 Constitution mandates the State to undertake a continuing program of urban land reform and housing which will make available at affordable cost decent housing and basic services to underprivileged and homeless citizens. Legislations, including Republic Act No. 9513 or the Renewable Energy Act of 2008, affirm the national policy to accelerate the utilization of renewable energy resources. However, despite existing policy frameworks, the integration of renewable energy systems, particularly solar home systems (SHS), into socialized housing developments remains largely dependent on project-level initiatives rather than a standardized national framework. This bill seeks to address the policy and implementation gap by mandating the integration of SHS in all socialized housing projects, whether on-grid, off-grid, or hybrid, and by establishing a dedicated financing mechanism to ensure its feasibility and affordability. By institutionalizing SHS as a standard component of housing design and delivery, this measure ensures that energy access is no longer treated as an auxiliary concern but as an essential element of housing adequacy. It likewise integrates the SHS Financing Program into housing amortization schemes with repayment terms of up to twenty-five (25) years, while employing a mix of subsidies, grants, and concessional financing to minimize the burden on beneficiary households. The financing structure is designed to ensure that total electricity-related expenditures remain comparable to, if not lower than, conventional grid-based electricity costs over time. The measure also establishes the technical standards, quality assurance mechanisms, and mandatory maintenance requirements to ensure system reliability and sustainability. It institutionalizes coordination among key agencies, including the Department of Human Settlements and Urban Development, Department of Energy, National Housing Authority, and Social Housing Finance Corporation, as well as Local Government Units, to ensure alignment in planning and execution. In addition, it provides for beneficiary orientation programs and a monitoring and evaluation system to track system performance, household energy savings, and broader socioeconomic and environmental impacts. Beyond ensuring energy adequacy, this measure promotes electricity security in socialized housing communities without adding strain to the national power grid. Additionally, where systems are grid-connected and eligible for net metering, these socialized housing communities may even contribute to the overall energy stability by serving as solar farms, supplying excess power back to the grid. The integration of solar energy systems in socialized housing represents a strategic shift toward building a climate-resilient, energy-secure, and sustainable communities, consistent with the State's commitment to inclusive development and environmental stewardship. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. LANI MERCADO-REVILLA ________ Baligad, J. (2024, May) Can't Take the Heat? title: AN ACT
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Education is one of the most powerful instruments for achieving inclusive and sustainable development. Access to quality higher education and technical- vocational training should not be limited by geographic location or economic circumstance. Students in geographically distant and underserved communities should likewise be given meaningful opportunities to pursue higher education and acquire the knowledge, skills, and competencies necessary to improve their lives and contribute to the development of their communities. Sultan Kudarat is a geographically expansive province with communities located at considerable distances from existing institutions of higher learning. For many students, particularly those coming from low-income families, the cost of transportation, board and lodging, and other expenses associated with studying outside their municipalities constitutes a significant barrier to obtaining a college education. Establishing campuses of the Sultan Kudarat State University (SKSU) in municipalities will substantially reduce these barriers and bring quality higher education closer to the people. This proposed measure seeks to establish campuses of the Sultan Kudarat State University (SKSU) in the Municipalities of Bagumbayan, Columbio, Esperanza, Lambayong, Lebak, President Quirino, Senator Ninoy Aquino, and SKSU-ACCESS in Tacurong City to expand access to affordable and quality higher education, technical-vocational training, research, extension services, and community development in these unserved municipalities. The proposed campuses shall primarily offer short-term, technical-vocational, undergraduate, and graduate programs consistent with their respective competencies, specializations, capabilities, and the standards prescribed by the Commission on Higher Education (CHED). Their programs shall be responsive to the human-resource requirements not only of the municipalities concerned but also of the Province of Sultan Kudarat and Region XII. The measure also further provides for the appointment or designation of Campus Director who shall be responsible for the effective administration and operation of the respective campuses, subject to the qualifications, standards, and guidelines prescribed by the University Board of Regents. It also requires compliance with the minimum requirements prescribed by CHED before the operation and program offerings of the campuses. The establishment of these provincial campuses is consistent with the constitutional policy of making quality education accessible to all and with the mandate of state universities and colleges to provide higher education, promote research and innovation, and extend their services to the communities they serve. More importantly, this measure will help ensure that the youth of Sultan Kudarat are given opportunities to obtain quality education without having to leave their respective municipalities merely to pursue their studies. It will also help develop a pool of competent professionals, skilled workers, researchers, entrepreneurs, teachers, and public servants who can contribute directly to the socioeconomic advancement of the Province of Sultan Kudarat and the SOCCSKSARGEN Region. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. » RUTH MANGUDADA AKALURAN Represent First District, Sultan Kudarat Representative Second District, Sultan Kudarat ONO KR WN = <e) PPAR HW WWWAHWWHWOW AN NNN NN NNN DND | |] B= Ba Bs a aa a a WBN HI OWA AN OO HhWNH HI TOA AN DOA RF WH H DHAWAN DOA WH =| OC Republic of the Philippines HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES Batasan Hills, Quezon City TWENTIETH CONGRESS First Regular Session HOUSEBILL NO. 11485 Introduced by: REP. title: AN ACT RECOGNIZING BAMBOO AS A HIGH-VALUE AND INDUSTRIAL CROP, FURTHER STRENGTHENING THE HIGH-VALUE CROPS DEVELOPMENT ACT BY INSTITUTIONALIZING THE NATIONAL HIGH- VALUE CROPS DEVELOPMENT AND BIOECONOMY PROGRAM, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7900, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “HIGH-VALUE CROPS DEVELOPMENT ACT OF 1995”” 22
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE 24 Republic Act No. 7900, or the High-Value Crops Development Act of 1995, established the national framework for the production, processing, marketing and distribution of high-value crops. Three decades later, climate change, biotechnology, plant-variety innovation, stricter product standards, supply-chain disruptions and growing demand for renewable and bio-based materials require a more integrated, science-based, market-oriented and institutionally sustained approach. 31 This bill expressly includes bamboo as a high-value crop and recognizes it as a strategic industrial crop. Bamboo can provide food, fiber, biomass, engineered and construction materials, furniture, packaging, bioenergy, biochar, biomaterials, and other value-added products. Developed through appropriate agroforestry and multi- storey farming systems, it can diversify rural livelihoods and support climate, soil, water, and ecosystem objectives, subject to environmental, biodiversity, land-use, agrarian reform and ancestral-domain laws. 39 The measure establishes within the Department of Agriculture the Office of the Undersecretary for High-Value Crops Development, Innovation, and Bioeconomy. The Office shall provide policy guidelines on technology management and innovation, exercise direct oversight over the National High-Value Crops and Bioeconomy Development Program, and supervise the functional roles, mandates and performance of its component offices. The bill also proposes the creation of one (1) Assistant Secretary position to support the Undersecretary and lead the agricultural statistics and data science, knowledge management, market intelligence, geospatial services, monitoring, evaluation and results reporting. A National High-Value Crops Program Management Office will be created and headed by Director position to coordinate implementation, provide technical services, farming systems, bamboo and industrial- crop development, agribusiness, processing, standards, investment, and markets. 13 The bill further integrates research, innovation, biotechnology, genetic resources, plant-variety development, quality planting materials, climate-resilient production, integrated development areas, processing, enterprise development, financing, standards, trade, and agricultural bioeconomy applications. It strengthens the High-Value Crops Development Fund and permits the Department to propose an indicative initial program envelope of Fifty Billion Pesos to support the five-year implementation of the act, subject to the regular budget process and without creating an automatic appropriation. 22 The proposed structure is designed as an integrating and coordinating mechanism. It preserves the statutory mandates of the Philippine Statistics Authority and other competent regulatory, research, standards, environmental, and local- government institutions, while requiring compliance with government-optimization, civil service, position-classification, budgeting, accounting and auditing laws. 28 In view of the foregoing, immediate approval of this measure is earnestly requested. 30 31 JOSE MANUEL F. title: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE PROTECTION, CONSERVATION, AND SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT OF THE SIERRA MADRE MOUNTAIN RANGE, CREATING FOR THE PURPOSE THE SIERRA MADRE MOUNTAIN RANGE AUTHORITY, DEFINING ITS POWERS AND FUNCTIONS, AND PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Sierra Madre Mountain Range is one of the Philippines’ most important natural assets. Stretching from Cagayan in the north to Quezon in the south, it forms a vast interconnected landscape of forests, watersheds, rivers, biodiversity areas, and coastal ecosystems. Its ecological functions extend far beyond the mountain range itself, providing essential services that sustain communities, agriculture, water systems, infrastructure, livelihoods, and economic activities in both upland and downstream areas. The Sierra Madre likewise serves as a critical natural defense against typhoons, flooding, landslides, storm surges, drought, and other climate-related hazards. Its forests, watersheds, wetlands, riparian areas, ecological corridors, and coastal ecosystems regulate water flows, store and sequester carbon, support biodiversity, and contribute to the resilience of communities and critical infrastructure. The protection and restoration of the Sierra Madre are therefore not merely matters of environmental conservation, but matters of national development, public safety, water security, climate resilience, and national security. Despite its importance, the Sierra Madre remains vulnerable to continuing degradation arising from illegal logging, destructive extraction, incompatible land conversion, habitat fragmentation, biodiversity loss, and other activities that undermine ecological integrity. Existing governmental mandates and management arrangements, while important, operate through different agencies, jurisdictions, plans, and regulatory systems. Such fragmentation makes it difficult to manage the Sierra Madre as one interconnected ecological system and to consistently account for impacts that cross administrative boundaries. This proposed measure seeks to address this institutional and ecological gap by establishing the Sierra Madre Mountain Range Authority (SMMRA) as a government- owned or -controlled corporation with an original charter, attached to the Office of the President for policy coordination and administrative supervision. The Authority is envisioned as the lead policy, planning, coordinating, and regulatory body for range-wide ecological governance, while preserving the lawful mandates of the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR), local government units, Protected Area Management Boards, the National Commission on Indigenous Peoples, and other competent institutions. At the center of the proposed framework is the Sierra Madre Ecological Integrity and Sustainable Development Master Plan, a comprehensive, science-based, geospatially explicit, 25-year plan that will establish ecological limits, management zones, no-go areas, permitted and prohibited uses, restoration priorities, measurable outcomes, investment requirements, and implementation responsibilities. The Master Plan will provide a common framework for harmonizing national, regional, local, ancestral-domain, and sectoral plans affecting the Sierra Madre. The measure adopts a landscape-scale and ridge-to-reef approach to conservation. Rather than treating forests, watersheds, rivers, biodiversity areas, and coastal ecosystems 1 as isolated units, the proposed framework recognizes their ecological and hydrological interdependence. It provides for the identification and protection of ecological corridors, riparian buffers, critical habitats, key biodiversity areas, and other connectivity systems necessary to maintain biodiversity and ecosystem resilience. The bill further advances a Nature-Based Solutions-First policy. Government interventions addressing flooding, landslides, erosion, watershed degradation, water insecurity, coastal hazards, and climate risks will be required to consider the feasibility of nature-based, green, or green-gray solutions before relying solely on conventional infrastructure. The proposed approach recognizes natural ecosystems as functional infrastructure capable of providing long-term disaster-risk reduction, water-security, and climate-adaptation benefits. Recognizing that conservation cannot be sustained without viable communities and economic incentives, the proposed measure promotes sustainable livelihoods, including agroforestry, ecotourism, and sustainable non-timber forest products. It also provides avenues for Indigenous Peoples, upland communities, and lawful tenure holders to participate in conservation and restoration activities and benefit from verified ecological outcomes. A significant innovation of the measure is the establishment of a Sierra Madre Nature Credit System. The system is intended to create a transparent and independently verified mechanism through which measurable protection, restoration, biodiversity, watershed, water- security, and climate-resilience outcomes may be recognized and financed. Covered enterprises that materially depend upon Sierra Madre ecosystem services may be required to satisfy Nature Credit Purchase Obligations, thereby helping align economic activity with the ecological services upon which such activity depends. The system expressly does not authorize prohibited activities or substitute for environmental, tenure, protected-area, or Indigenous Peoples safeguards. To support the long-term implementation of the law, the bill establishes a Sierra Madre Fund and provides for lawful and transparent financing mechanisms, including national government appropriations, certain environmental charges, penalties and restoration recoveries when legally assignable, grants and technical assistance, and other lawful sources. The Fund is limited to the Authority’s statutory public-good and market-governance functions and is subject to government accounting, procurement, auditing, transparency, and disclosure requirements. title: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE EXTENSION OF TERMS OF PROTECTION OF COPYRIGHT AND RELATED RIGHTS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTIONS 213 AND 215 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8293, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE "INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES"
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines, or Republic Act No. 8293, provides protection to authors, performers, producers of sound recordings, and broadcasting organizations for their creative works and contributions. The existing law provides specific periods of protection for copyright and related rights, which this measure seeks to strengthen in view of the continuing development of the creative and digital industries. This measure seeks to extend the period of copyright protection for works covered under Sections 172 and 173 of Republic Act No. 8293 from fifty (50) years to seventy-five (75) years. It likewise extends the protection for photographic works and audio-visual works to seventy-five (75) years. For performers and producers of sound recordings, the period of protection is similarly proposed to be extended from fifty (50) years to seventy-five (75) years. The protection granted to broadcasting organizations is also proposed to be increased from twenty (20) years to fifty (50) years. The extension of these terms will provide Filipino authors, performers, producers, and other rights holders with a longer period within which they may benefit from their creative works. For performers and producers, in particular, a longer period of protection will allow them to continue receiving economic benefits from works that may remain commercially valuable for many years after their creation or initial release. It will likewise provide rights holders greater opportunity to recover investments made in the creation, production, marketing, and distribution of creative works. By strengthening the period of protection granted to creative works and related rights, this measure seeks to provide greater incentives for the creation, dissemination, preservation, and continued commercial exploitation of Filipino works. It will likewise contribute to the development of the Philippine creative industry, encourage investment in creative works, and help ensure that Filipino creators and rights holders continue to benefit from their intellectual and artistic contributions. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. RUFUS B. RODRIGUEZ MAXIMOB.B.RODRIGUEZ, MAXIMO RODRIGUEZ,JR. JR. title: AN ACT MANDATING THE RECRUITMENT, HIRING, AND TRAINING OF SCHOOL-BASED LICENSED GUIDANCE COUNSELORS, PSYCHOLOGISTS, SCHOOL SOCIAL WORKERS AND MENTAL HEALTH PERSONNEL
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The mental health and psychosocial well-being of students are essential to their ability to learn, develop, and participate meaningfully in school and community life. Schools are often among the first places where behavioral, emotional, social, and psychological difficulties among children and young people may be identified. This measure seeks to provide public elementary and secondary schools with additional personnel who can provide counseling, psychosocial support, early intervention, referral, and other appropriate services to students. It likewise recognizes the important role of teachers, school personnel, and parents in identifying concerns and supporting the overall well-being of students. By strengthening the availability of qualified professionals within schools, the proposed Act aims to address mental, emotional, behavioral, and psychosocial concerns at an earlier stage and help create a more supportive learning environment. The measure therefore provides for the recruitment and training of appropriate school-based personnel, establishes supervision and service guidelines, and provides the necessary funding through the annual General Appropriations Act. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this measure is earnestly sought. CHARISSE ANNE C. title: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE RIGHTS OF PATIENTS AGAINST HOSPITAL DETENTION ON THE GROUND OF NONPAYMENT OF HOSPITAL BILLS AND MEDICAL EXPENSES AND PROVIDING STIFFER PENALTIES FOR VIOLATION THEREFOR, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 9439, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS “AN ACT PROHIBITING THE DETENTION OF PATIENTS IN HOSPITALS AND MEDICAL CLINICS ON GROUNDS OF NONPAYMENT OF HOSPITAL BILLS OR MEDICAL EXPENSES”
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Patients should not be deprived of their liberty, nor should their families be prevented from securing their release or obtaining necessary medical documents, solely because of their inability to immediately settle hospital bills and medical expenses. Republic Act No. 9439, otherwise known as the “Anti-Hospital Detention Law”, was enacted to protect patients from being detained in hospitals and medical clinics on account of unpaid hospital bills or medical expenses. Despite the protection provided by law, cases continue to arise where patients and their families experience difficulty securing discharge, obtaining medical documents, or claiming benefits. There is therefore a need to strengthen the safeguards provided under the law and ensure that its protections are effectively implemented. This measure seeks to expressly prohibit the detention of patients, their relatives, representatives, or caregivers, as well as the withholding of newborn children, solely on account of unpaid hospital bills, medical expenses, or professional fees. It likewise seeks to ensure the prompt release of the remains of deceased patients and the timely issuance of the necessary documents. The bill further provides reasonable mechanisms by which financially incapacitated patients may secure their unpaid obligations. The enactment of this measure will strengthen the protection of patients and their families, promote humane and dignified treatment in health facilities, and ensure that inability to immediately pay for medical treatment does not become a ground for unlawful detention or withholding of essential documents. For these reasons, the immediate passage of this bill is urgently sought. REP. EDUARDO R. title: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING A COMPREHENSIVE SCHOOL SAFETY FRAMEWORK, ENSURING THE SAFETY AND WELL-BEING OF LEARNERS AND SCHOOL PERSONNEL, AND PROMOTING A SAFE AND SUPPORTIVE SCHOOL COMMUNITY
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Every learner has the right to study in an environment that is safe, healthy, inclusive, and supportive. Schools should not only provide quality education but also protect learners and school personnel from violence, abuse, bullying, discrimination, harassment, disasters, health emergencies, and other threats to their safety and well-being. The continuing prevalence of violence and bullying among children underscores the need to strengthen school safety measures. The 2015 National Baseline Study on Violence Against Children, conducted by the Council for the Welfare of Children and UNICEF, found that 65% of Filipino children and youth aged 13 to 24 experienced peer violence, while 64.2% experienced physical violence and 61.5% experienced psychological violence during childhood. More recently, the Department of Education reported 2,500 bullying cases in the National Capital Region during School Year 2024–2025, demonstrating that bullying and violence continue to pose significant concerns within the school environment. These circumstances show that school safety must go beyond physical security. It must also address the mental, emotional, psychosocial, and digital well-being of learners and school personnel. With the increasing use of digital technologies, schools must likewise be prepared to address cyberbullying, online abuse, cybersecurity risks, and other emerging threats. This measure seeks to institutionalize a Comprehensive School Safety Framework for public and private basic education institutions. It provides common standards for the prevention of risks, preparedness for emergencies, response to incidents, and recovery and support for affected members of the school community. Under the proposed measure, every school shall develop a School Safety Plan and maintain a School Safety Handbook containing appropriate procedures for emergency response, learner protection, reporting and referral, mental health and psychosocial support, digital safety, disaster preparedness, and off-campus activities. The bill also strengthens the roles of school personnel and promotes coordination among the Department of Education, Department of Health, Department of Social Welfare and Development, Department of the Interior and Local Government, Philippine National Police, local government units, and other concerned agencies and stakeholders. It further provides for appropriate safety infrastructure, risk assessments, emergency drills, disaster preparedness, and mechanisms for addressing bullying, abuse, violence, discrimination, and other threats. By establishing a unified and preventive approach to school safety, this measure seeks to ensure that schools are equipped not only to respond to incidents, but also to identify and prevent risks before they result in harm. Ultimately, a safe learning environment is essential to quality education. Protecting learners and school personnel from violence, hazards, and other threats will allow schools to better fulfill their fundamental role in developing healthy, capable, and resilient Filipino children and youth. In view of the foregoing, the immediate approval of this bill is earnestly sought. ANTOLIN “LENLEN” A. title: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE FILIPINO FAMILY AS THE FOUNDATION OF THE NATION, INSTITUTIONALIZING FAMILY-CENTERED GOVERNANCE, ESTABLISHING MECHANISMS FOR THE PROTECTION, DEVELOPMENT, AND WELL-BEING OF FILIPINO FAMILIES, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Constitution recognizes the Filipino family as the foundation of the nation and commands the State to strengthen its solidarity and actively promote its total development. It further recognizes marriage as an inviolable social institution and the foundation of the family, protects the right of spouses to found a family according to their religious convictions and the demands of responsible parenthood, affirms the natural and primary right and duty of parents in the rearing of the youth, protects the rights of children, and equally protects the life of the mother and the life of the unborn from conception. These guarantees reflect a fundamental principle of a free and humane society: the dignity of the person is ordinarily first encountered, recognized, protected and developed within the family. The family is more than an aggregation of individuals receiving separate government services. It is a community of persons joined by enduring relationships of marriage, parenthood, filiation, kinship, responsibility, care and mutual support. It is where children first experience belonging and formation, where parents assume primary responsibility for their upbringing, where generations care for one another, and where citizens first learn responsibility, solidarity and participation in society. The rights of persons and the integrity of the family therefore reinforce one another. The State must protect every individual from violence, abuse, exploitation and neglect while, at the same time, respecting the legitimate autonomy of family life and supporting families in the discharge of responsibilities that properly belong to them. This balance requires the principle of subsidiarity. Public authorities should assist families when assistance is needed, coordinate with communities and civil society when these can effectively respond, and intervene directly when protection or the public welfare requires it. Government should strengthen legitimate family functions rather than unnecessarily displace them. This principle is especially important today. Filipino families face increasingly complex economic, social and cultural pressures. Household size continues to decline. Marriage is occurring later and less frequently. Fertility has fallen below replacement level. Millions of families experience prolonged separation because of overseas or internal migration. Parents confront growing demands involving work, caregiving, education, technology, mental health and child protection. Grandparents increasingly 2 perform caregiving responsibilities. Poor and vulnerable families frequently navigate several government agencies merely to address problems experienced simultaneously within one household. Government possesses numerous family-related statutes and programs, yet these interventions remain dispersed across institutions organized according to administrative mandates rather than around the family that experiences these conditions as one reality. This bill therefore establishes a permanent national system of family- centered governance. It creates the National Commission on the Filipino Family, supported by a National Advisory Council and a professional Secretariat, as the principal policy, coordinating, monitoring and standards-setting institution for family-centered governance. It establishes a National Filipino Family Development Framework, measurable family well-being indicators, proportionate Family Impact Assessments for major government measures, local family-service convergence, and mechanisms for accountability and periodic evaluation. The bill recognizes the family as a subject of legitimate interests and participation while fully respecting the constitutional and statutory rights of each family member. It preserves the Family Code and expressly avoids altering marriage, filiation, parental authority, support, succession, property relations and other matters of substantive family law by implication. The measure strengthens marriage preparation and voluntary accompaniment during the early years of married life; expands parenting and family-formation services; promotes responsible fatherhood and motherhood; strengthens family-school cooperation and parental participation in education; 3 integrates family support with maternal and child health and early childhood services; and reinforces protection of children and other vulnerable family members. It also recognizes that work and family life are inseparable dimensions of human development. Families require adequate income and conditions of employment that allow parents and carers to perform their responsibilities. The bill therefore integrates family economic security, work-family balance, caregiving, housing, nutrition and social protection into the national family- policy framework. Consistent with the Constitution, the measure affirms the inherent dignity of every human being and the equal protection of the life of the mother and the unborn from conception. It strengthens prenatal, maternal and early-childhood support, particularly during the first one thousand days of life, while preserving existing laws governing legal personality, health services and family relations. It further recognizes solidarity with the weakest as an essential responsibility of society. Poor families, children, senior citizens, persons with disabilities, solo parents, families affected by migration, disaster or displacement, and persons threatened by violence, abuse or exploitation require particular attention. At the same time, solidarity must strengthen rather than create unnecessary dependence. Public assistance should, whenever reasonably possible, increase the capacity of families and communities to care for their members and participate fully in economic and civic life. title: AN ACT REGISTERING AND REGULATING SOCIAL MEDIA PLATFORMS
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The proliferation of social media platforms has revolutionized the way Filipinos communicate, access information, and participate in public discourse. These platforms have become essential tools for education, business, governance, and social interaction. However, the rapid expansion and influence of social media have also brought challenges, including the spread of misinformation, hate speech, cyberbullying, privacy violations, and other harmful online behaviors that threaten public order and individual rights. The Social Media Platform Regulation Act of 2026 seeks to establish a comprehensive legal framework to regulate social media platforms operating in the Philippines. This legislation aims to balance the protection of freedom of expression and innovation with the need to ensure accountability, transparency, and the safety of users in the digital space. The key provisions of the bill include: ● The establishment of clear guidelines for the operation of social media platforms to prevent the dissemination of harmful content such as fake news, hate speech, and illegal activities; ● Requirements for transparency in content moderation policies and algorithms used by social media companies; ● Safeguards to protect user privacy and data security; ● Mechanisms for prompt and effective response to complaints and grievances from users; ● Promotion of digital literacy and responsible online behavior among Filipinos; ● Strengthening the cooperation between the government, social media platforms, and civil society to foster a safer and more accountable online environment. This bill seeks to address that gap by mandating the registration and regulation of social media platforms operating in the Philippines, especially those with a significant user base or content reach in the country. It aims to ensure that these platforms observe standards of transparency, cooperate with government agencies in identifying sources of fake news, and implement robust mechanisms to detect and take down harmful content without infringing on constitutionally protected freedoms. It also seeks to promote accountability and discourage the spread of false information by imposing heavy fines and criminal prosecution, ensuring that addressing national and global issues is not hindered by disinformation. By enacting this law, the State reaffirms its commitment to uphold the constitutional rights of every Filipino while adapting to the evolving challenges posed by digital technologies. It ensures that social media platforms contribute positively to nation-building, democracy, and social cohesion. In view of the foregoing, the passage of this bill is earnestly sought. HON. ATTY. title: AN ACT EXTENDING THE CORPORATE LIFE OF THE PHILIPPINE INTERNATIONAL TRADING CORPORATION (PITC) FOR ANOTHER TWENTY FIVE YEARS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 2 OF PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 1071, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS “THE REVISED CHARTER OF THE PHILIPPINE INTERNATIONAL TRADING CORPORATION”
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Philippine International Trading Corporation (PITC) was created through Presidential Decree No. 252, and its charter was subsequently revised by Presidential Decree No. 1071, otherwise known as the “Revised Charter of the Philippine International Trading Corporation.” Under Section 2 of Presidential Decree No. 1071, the Corporation is authorized to exist for a period of fifty (50) years, with its present corporate term set to expire on 25 January 2027. For several decades, PITC has served as a government corporate vehicle in pursuing the State’s objectives in international trade. Consistent with its charter, the Corporation has undertaken trade-related activities and provided services intended to facilitate international trade, promote Philippine products and enterprises, and support the Government in its foreign procurement and marketing activities. As the expiration of PITC’s corporate term approaches, there is a need to ensure the continuity of its juridical personality, operations, and existing commitments. The expiration of its corporate term without an appropriate legislative measure may create uncertainty regarding the Corporation’s authority to continue performing its lawful functions, administering its assets and liabilities, honoring its contractual commitments, and undertaking transactions necessary for the fulfillment of its mandate. The proposed measure seeks to address this concern by providing for the continued corporate existence of PITC, while ensuring that such continued existence remains subject to appropriate government oversight and accountability. The proposed framework recognizes that the continued existence of a government- owned or -controlled corporation must be accompanied by mechanisms for periodic assessment of its relevance, efficiency, financial viability, performance, and consistency with national development policies and priorities. Accordingly, the GCG may conduct periodic performance evaluation and oversight of PITC, taking into account, among others, its financial performance, operational efficiency, governance and risk management systems, delivery of services, and contribution to the promotion and development of Philippine international trade. The measure further recognizes that perpetual corporate existence does not exempt PITC from continuing government evaluation, oversight, and accountability. The Corporation shall remain subject to the evaluation, monitoring, and other appropriate actions authorized under Republic Act No. 10149, otherwise known as the “GOCC Governance Act of 2011,” and other applicable laws, rules, and regulations. Where warranted by such evaluation and consistent with applicable law, the appropriate government authorities may undertake or recommend such lawful measures as may be necessary to ensure that the Corporation remains relevant, efficient, financially viable, and responsive to the national interest. The grant of perpetual existence is not intended to constitute a determination that the Corporation shall operate indefinitely regardless of its continued relevance, performance, or economic viability. Rather, PITC shall remain subject to the performance evaluation, monitoring, and oversight mechanisms applicable to government-owned or -controlled corporations under Republic Act No. 10149 and other applicable laws. At the same time, the proposed measure does not seek to expand the substantive powers and functions of PITC under Presidential Decree No. 1071. Rather, it seeks to ensure the continuity of the Corporation’s juridical personality and operations while strengthening accountability and providing for continuing evaluation by the appropriate government authorities. The proposed perpetual corporate term will also eliminate the need for periodic legislative action solely for the purpose of extending the Corporation’s corporate existence, while preserving the authority of Congress to amend, repeal, or otherwise modify the Corporation’s charter or corporate existence through subsequent legislation. This approach provides greater institutional stability and continuity while maintaining the necessary safeguards to ensure that PITC remains relevant, efficient, financially viable, and responsive to the national interest. Perpetual corporate existence does not preclude the State from undertaking performance evaluation, monitoring, and oversight of the Corporation's relevance, performance, efficiency, and financial viability, nor does it prevent the appropriate government authorities from recommending or undertaking such lawful measures as may be warranted by the results of such evaluation. The continued corporate existence of PITC is therefore intended to prevent disruption in its legal existence and operations and to ensure the orderly continuity of its contracts, obligations, assets, liabilities, and other lawful commitments. It will likewise enable the Corporation to continue performing its existing mandate and contributing, within the scope of its charter, to the promotion and development of Philippine international trade. In view of the foregoing, immediate approval of this measure is earnestly requested. RUFUS B. RODRIGUEZ MAXIMO B. RODRIGUEZ, JR.
