title: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE PROTECTION AND WELFARE OF ANIMALS, CREATING FOR THE PURPOSE THE NATIONAL COMMISSION ON ANIMAL WELFARE, AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8485, AS AMENDED, PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATIONS THEREOF, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The Animal Welfare Act of 1998 (Republic Act No. 8485), as amended in 2013, was a landmark in Philippine law — the first to impose criminal liability for acts of cruelty against animals. However, more than a decade of enforcement has proven that the law is no longer equal to the scale of the problem. Institutional authority over animal welfare remains fragmented, penalties are weak and undifferentiated, population management tools are absent, and accountability for government-run facilities is virtually nonexistent.1 Science has also advanced. International standards now recognize animals as sentient beings capable of suffering, fear, and positive emotional states. Animal welfare policy is now based on the Five Domains framework: nutrition, physical environment, health, behavioral expression, and mental state.2 Philippine law has not kept pace. The gap between law and reality is stark. According to a report issued by Mars 1 World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH), Terrestrial Animal Health Code, Chapters 7.1–7.8 (Animal Welfare); Universal Declaration on Animal Welfare (UDAW), adopted by the World Society for the Protection of Animals. 2 D.J. Mellor, “Updating Animal Welfare Thinking: Moving beyond the ‘Five Freedoms’ towards ‘A Life Worth Living’,” Animals, Vol. 6, No. 3 (2016), p. 21. Petcare in 2024, there are 13 million stray cats and dogs in the Philippines.3 Despite the fact that a majority of Philippine households have at least one pet in their domestic residence,4 animal welfare has received little priority in State policy and government programs. Worse, in 2020, the Care and Responsibility for Animals (CARA) Welfare Philippines, Inc. reported 3,000 cases of animal abuse, including beating, kicking, and mutilating.5 Hence, this Bill, which is an overhaul of the Animal Welfare Act of 1998. It anchors Philippine policy on the Five Domains of Animal Welfare and the Philippines’ international commitments, including the Convention on Biological Diversity and the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species.6 It replaces a weak and scattered enforcement architecture with a single empowered agency, and it closes the legal loopholes that have allowed cruelty to go unpunished. Specifically, this Bill seeks to: (1) Replace the Committee on Animal Welfare with a National Commission on Animal Welfare, an independent and autonomous quasi-judicial agency with full fiscal autonomy, rule-making authority, licensing and enforcement powers, and the mandate to facilitate all efforts in prosecuting animal cruelty cases;7 (2) Mandate local government units to establish dedicated personnel with their local government veterinarians, deploy fully capacitated and trained personnel, and implement Trap-Neuter-Vaccinate-Return programs as the primary, humane method of controlling stray animal populations;8 (3) Impose strict public accountability on pounds, including mandatory spay- neuter prior to release, publicly accessible impoundment records, and minimum operating hours open to the public; (4) Prohibit animal experimentation in elementary schools and require all secondary and tertiary institutions to adhere to global standards in the preservation and care of animals, such as the internationally recognized 3Rs Principle (Replacement, Reduction, Refinement);9 3 Zaldarriaga, Joe. “The Private Sector and Animal Welfare.” Philippine News Agency, February 17, 2025. <https://www.pna.gov.ph/opinion/pieces/1014-the-private-sector-and-animal-welfare> 4 Id. 5 Wang, Mel. “Inside The Never-Ending Fight Against Animal Abuse In The Philippines” – Rolling Stone Philippines, October 6, 2025. https://rollingstonephilippines.com/state-of-affairs/animal-rights-abuse-philippines/ 6 Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD), 1992; Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES), 1973, to which the Philippines is a State Party. 7 RA 8485, Sec. 1, as amended by RA 10631, constitutes the Committee on Animal Welfare (CAW) under the Department of Agriculture. 8 Trap-Neuter-Vaccinate-Return (TNVR) is endorsed by the World Health Organization and WOAH as an evidence-based, humane method of managing free-roaming dog and cat populations. See WHO/WSPA, Guidelines for Dog Population Management (1990). 9 The 3Rs Principle was articulated by W.M.S. Russell and R.L. title: AN ACT MANDATING THE ASSIGNMENT OF AN AGRICULTURAL TECHNICIAN IN EACH LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNIT AND ENHANCING THE OPERATIONAL CAPABILITIES OF THE TECHNICIANS THEREOF
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Agriculture used to be one of the Philippines’ strongest sectors in the economy. We prided ourselves with the ability of our farmers to compete in the global market. However, present times show a completely different picture. What used to be a robust agricultural sector now has given way to other sectors such as the services and manufacturing sector. From exporters of products such as rice, we now import rice to be able to feed our growing population. But the agricultural sector should not be left to decline, in fact it may present the solution to many of our economic woes. A boosted agricultural sector would help us with food security issues. If agriculture becomes economically viable, rural economies would undergo a drastic transformation. Farmers would no longer have to venture into cities to find work, thereby reducing rural-urban migration. This in turn would lead to decongested cities and reduce the pressure to create more and more jobs in urban environments. This is why we need to inculcate advancements made in agricultural technology with our farmers. While there exist programs that already seek to impart such knowledge directly to our farmers, its effects may be attained faster and in greater magnitude if there is an assigned an expert in agricultural technology that routinely aids and assesses each farmer’s yield and capabilities. It is for these foregoing premises that approval of this bill is earnestly sought. ALFRED C. Of this group, 5 million (or 4.7 percent) are aged 65 and older. Elderly abuse has unfortunately become a full-blown social cancer in the Philippines:3 Physical abuse are acts that are committed with intention of causing physical pain and injury. It can be in the form of being hit, sexually assaulted or burned. Any act leading to physical or bodily pain (i.e. bruises, sprains, welts, abrasions and fractures) and injury is classified under this. Psychological or emotional abuse involves verbal assaults, threats, humiliation, and ridicule. Such abuse is usually accompanied by physical abuse but may happen separately. Material or financial abuse includes misuse of property or money, theft, or forced signing of legal documents. Neglect may be referred to as passive or unintentional and active or intentional. Passive or unintentional neglect would mean isolation of the elderly or the elderly are left alone. The family, because of other duties, may not be able to meet the needs of the elderly or the caregiver is incompetent to provide care for the elderly. Active or intentional neglect involves the deliberate withholding of items needed for daily living (food, medicine, companionship and care) especially from those who are physically dependent. xxx A. Moreover being single and widowed is another factor adding to their susceptible condition. Being dependent on the family, unfortunately, in a way has become a disadvantage as well. For some families, they see the state of the elderly as an opportunity to take over whatever wealth the elderly has and deliberately neglecting or ignoring the elderly. Financial abuse is one of the frequent complaints accompanied by physical abuse. The children who still live with their parents, either employed or unemployed are oftentimes the perpetrators or abusers. The abusers extort money from them to support their needs or expenses, failure of the elderly to give money usually leads to physical abuse. title: AN ACT INCREASING THE MONTHLY SALARY AND OTHER BENEFITS OF HEALTH WORKERS IN THE PHILIPPINES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The experiences of the COVID-19 Pandemic in the Philippines left a lasting mark and a vital lesson. The country, as well as the globe entire, were caught lacking and unready to deal with a health emergency of such size. Although not unprecedented in recent human history, the pandemic was unique in its scale and disruption in living memory. It is a grim reality, warned by medical experts, scientists, and historians alike, that such a global pandemic will not be the last. It most assuredly will happen again. As such, the COVID-19 pandemic serves as a wake-up call. For our government, its instruments, and our precarious health care system, capacities must be expanded, processes must be streamlined, and bureaucracy must be made more efficient. A strong healthcare system likewise relies on its greatest resource: human resources, or the health workers that are on the frontline of such health emergencies. Without competent members of the healthcare profession comprising our public health system, we cannot expect that our public healthcare will be able to sustain and provide quality healthcare for all Filipinos. As such, it is of utmost importance that they be given the appreciation and benefits they deserve, in light of their significance in Philippine society. It is then incumbent for us to increase their salary and benefits considering the risks that their employment poses. It is for these reasons that the passage of this bill is earnestly sought In view of the foregoing, the passage of this measure is urgently sought. ALFRED C. title: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE CONSTRUCTION OF A BRIDGE OR UNDERSEA TUNNEL LINKING THE PROVINCE OF CEBU AND THE PROVINCE OF NEGROS ORIENTAL, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Cebu and Negros Island are linked by sea, but travel and the movement of goods between them remain dependent on maritime crossings. A permanent link would improve connectivity within Central Visayas, facilitate the movement of people and goods, and create new opportunities for trade, tourism, investment, and regional development. It would also provide an additional transport option when sea crossings are unavailable or disrupted. This bill provides for the construction of a bridge or undersea tunnel connecting the Municipality of Santander, Cebu, and the Municipality of Sibulan, Negros Oriental. The proposed project would establish a direct and continuous land transport connection between Cebu Island and Negros Island, subject to the results of comprehensive feasibility, engineering, environmental, and other necessary technical studies. The project must consider not only the bridge or tunnel crossing itself, but also the necessary approach roads, interchanges, and connections to the existing road networks of Cebu and Negros Oriental. These components must be planned and developed as an integrated transport corridor to ensure that the completed link provides safe, efficient, and convenient movement between the two islands. The proposed link would make travel between Cebu and Negros Oriental easier and more efficient, provide a more direct route for the movement of goods, and improve access to essential services, employment centers, and economic opportunities. It could also strengthen disaster response and emergency mobility by providing another route for personnel, equipment, relief supplies, and other essential resources between the two islands. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. MARCELINO C. title: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE CONSTRUCTION OF A BRIDGE OR UNDERSEA TUNNEL LINKING THE PROVINCE OF SOUTHERN LEYTE AND THE PROVINCE OF BOHOL, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Southern Leyte and Bohol are linked by sea, but travel and the movement of goods between them remain dependent on maritime crossings. A permanent link would improve access between Eastern and Central Visayas and create new opportunities for trade, tourism, and investment. It would also provide another transport option when sea crossings are unavailable. This bill provides for the construction of a bridge or undersea tunnel following a proposed alignment from Maasin City, Southern Leyte, through Lapinig Island, Bohol to Ubay, Bohol. It would establish a continuous land route across the two water crossings, subject to the results of feasibility and engineering studies. Lapinig Island serves as an intermediate point in the proposed route. Accordingly, the project must consider the connections between Maasin City and Lapinig Island, between Lapinig Island and Ubay, and across the island itself. Examining these sections together is necessary to ensure that the completed link functions as one practical transport corridor. The proposed link would make travel between Southern Leyte and Bohol easier, provide a more direct route for the movement of goods, and improve access to essential services. It could also strengthen disaster response by giving emergency personnel, equipment, and relief supplies another route between the two provinces when conditions permit. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. MARCELINO C. title: AN ACT MANDATING THE DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH (DOH) TO ENSURE THE AVAILABILITY OF MEDICINES AND PROCUREMENT OF MEDICAL EQUIPMENT IN ALL PUBLIC HOSPITALS THROUGH THE UTILIZATION OF THE MEDICAL ASSISTANCE TO INDIGENT AND FINANCIALLY INCAPACITATED PATIENTS (MAIFIP) FUND.
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The 1987 Philippine Constitution mandates the State to protect aud promote the right to health of the people and instill health consciousness among them. Despite this constitutional guarantee, many public hospitals across the country continue to grapple with chronic shortages of essential medicines and a lack of basic diagnostic equipment. This reality places a heavy burden on indigent and financially incapacitated Filipinos who rely entirely on government healthcare facilities for their survival and well-being. This proposed measure seeks to address this critical gap by institutionalizing a proactive and sustainable procurement mechanism. It mandates the Department of Health (DOH) to ensure a continuous, adequate supply of essential medicines and guarantees that all public hospitals are equipped with baseline diagnostic tools like functional X-ray, ultrasound, and ECG machines. To ensure the viability of this mandate, the bill introduces a strategic funding approach. It maximizes the existing Medical Assistance to Indigent and Financially Incapacitated Patients (MAIFIP) Fund by explicitly earmarking at least twenty-five percent (25%) of its annual allocation exclusively for the procurement of essential medicines and medical equipment. By converting a portion of direct financial assistance into tangible, readily available healthcare resources at the point of care, the government can prevent stockouts, lower overall healthcare costs through bulk procurement, and provide immediate diagnostic and medical relief to marginalized patients. Furthermore, the bill institutes safeguards for transparency, efficient inventory management, and regular congressional reporting to ensure that the funds are utilized effectively and reach the Filipinos who need them most. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. REP. PHILIY CONRAD “DOK BONG” M. title: AN ACT MANDATING TO PROFESSIONALIZE AND ELEVATE STERILE PROCESSING AS A CRITICAL COMPONENT OF HEALTHCARE QUALITY AND PATIENT SAFETY, AND DEVELOP THE INTERNATIONAL STANDARDS, RESOURCES AND BEST PRACTICES IN STERILIZATION SCIENCES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Article II, Section 15 of the 1987 Philippine Constitution declares that “The State shall protect and promote the right to health of the people and instill health consciousness among them.” Central to this mandate is the guarantee of patient safety and the delivery of high-quality healthcare services in all medical facilities across the country. Despite advancements in medical technology, Healthcare-Associated Infections (HAIs) remain a persistent and life-threatening risk to patients. A critical vulnerability in infection control is the improper cleaning, decontamination, and sterilization of reusable medical devices and hospital workspaces. The emergence of highly resilient pathogens, such as prions, and the increasing complexity of surgical instruments necessitate a rigorous, scientifically backed approach to infection control that leaves no room for error. Currently, there is a need to professionalize and standardize stcrile processing as a distinct, highly regulated discipline within the Philippine healthcare system. The Central Sterile Services Department (CSSD) is the beating heart of hospital infection control, yet standardizing its operations to meet rigorous international benchmarks requires dedicated legislative backing. This bill seeks to elevate sterilization sciences by requiring all health care facilities, whether government or private, hospital or office-based clinic, to secure a specialized “Sterile Permit” prior to operation. To achieve this, the proposed measure: 1. Establishes Strict Regulatory Standards: Mandates health care facilities to submit detailed operational plans for decontamination, disinfection, and sterilization based on international best practices, including the Spaulding Classification System. 2. Empowers the Department of Health: Designates the Health Facilities and Services Regulatory Bureau (HFSRB) as the licensing agency tasked with inspecting facilities, issuing permits, monitoring HAI rates, and enforcing compliance. 3. Professionalizes the Workspace and Workforce: Requires dedicated architectural spaces for decontamination and _ sterile storage, specialized equipment like medical washers, strict use of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE), and concrete protocols for process failures and occupational exposure. 4. Protects Healthcare Workers: Integrates occupational satety measures and transmission-based precautions to shield the personnel handling bioburden and hazardous materials daily. By treating sterile processing not merely as a hospital support service, but as a critical, highly specialized component of patient survival, we can drastically reduce preventable infections, protect our frontline healthcare workers, and align Philippine medical facilities with global health standards. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. REP. PHI CONRAD “DOK BONG” M. title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A NATIONAL HEALTHCARE SAFETY AND RELIABILITY SYSTEM, THEREBY CREATING THE NATIONAL HEALTHCARE SAFETY AUTHORITY (NHSA), AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Article II, Section 15 of the 1987 Philippine Constitution mandates that “The State shall protect and promote the right to health of the people and instill health consciousness among them.” While significant strides have been made to expand healthcare access across the country, access alone is insufficient if the care provided is unsafe. Preventable medical harm, adverse events, and systemic errors remain a significant but often underreported threat to public health and national development. Currently, the approach to medical errors in the healthcare sector is heavily punitive. This environment discourages healthcare workers from reporting near-misses and adverse events out of fear of administrative, civil, or criminal retaliation. Without transparent reporting, the healthcare system loses critical opportunities to analyze root causes, correct systemic flaws, and prevent future harm. The proposed bill mandates the creation of the National Healthcare Safety Authority (NHSA), an independent body attached to the Department of Health (DOH). The NHSA will be tasked with developing mandatory national patient safety standards, conducting safety audits, and establishing a confidential, non-punitive national incident reporting system. By legally protecting good-faith reporters, the State empowers healthcare professionals to become active partners in identifying systemic risks without the fear of unjust reprisal. Furthermore, this bill introduces a public Healthcare Safety Rating System to empower patients with transparent data regarding facility compliance and safety outcomes. It also mandates the integration of these safety metrics into PhilHealth’s accreditation and reimbursement systems, ensuring that public funds are directed toward institutions that prioritize high-quality, reliable care. Healthcare must be designed to heal, not harm. By establishing a dedicated authority and a proactive, evidence-based framework for patient safety, this legislation will strengthen public trust in our medical institutions and ensure that every Filipino receives the safe, high-quality healthcare they deserve. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. REP. PHI CONRAD “DOK BONG” M. title: AN ACT REQUIRING THE TEACHING OF BASIC ROAD SAFETY AND COMPREHENSIVE DRIVERS' EDUCATION AS PART OF THE CURRICULUM OF THE K-12 PROGRAM, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Road safety is a pressing public health and education concern. The World Health Organization’s Global Status Report on Road Safety (2023) highlights that road traffic injuries remain the leading cause of death among people aged 5 to 29 worldwide. In the Philippines, the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) reported over 11,000 road crash fatalities in 2022, while Metro Manila alone recorded more than 65,000 road accidents in the same year. These alarming figures underscore the need for a preventive approach through early education. By integrating Basic Road Safety and Comprehensive Drivers’ Education into the K-12 curriculum, students will gain practical knowledge on traffic rules, pedestrian rights, commuter etiquette, and defensive driving principles. The inclusion of a Monitoring and Evaluation mechanism ensures accountability and continuous improvement, allowing policymakers to track outcomes such as reduced youth-related road incidents and improved safety awareness. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. ATTY. title: AN ACT INCREASING CAMPUS SECURITY AND CRIME AWARENESS BY INSTALLING CLOSED-CIRCUIT TELEVISION (CCTV) CAMERAS AND WALK- THROUGH METAL DETECTORS IN ALL SCHOOLS AND PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Schools are meant to be sanctuaries of learning where students, teachers, and school personnel can thrive without fear of violence or disruption. However, educational institutions remain vulnerable to various threats that may compromise safety, disrupt learning, and undermine the right of every learner to a secure educational environment. This bill seeks to strengthen and institutionalize school security nationwide by mandating the installation of Closed-Circuit Television (CCTV) cameras and walk-through metal detectors in all schools. CCTV cameras will enhance monitoring, incident documentation, and crime prevention, while metal detectors will serve as a preventive measure against the entry of firearms, bladed weapons, and other dangerous objects into school premises. The measure also requires coordination among the Department of Education (DepEd), Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG), Philippine National Police (PNP), and Local Government Units (LGUs) to ensure the proper deployment, maintenance, and operation of these security measures. Schools may likewise be prioritized based on risk assessment and other relevant security considerations. By institutionalizing these measures, the State affirms its responsibility to protect the lives and welfare of students, teachers, and school personnel. Ensuring a safe and secure school environment is essential to sustaining quality education and allowing learners to study, grow, and develop without fear. This legislation is a proactive and long-term measure to strengthen school safety and prevent violence and other security threats within educational institutions. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. ATTY. title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A SAFETY INTERNET EDUCATION PROGRAM IN THE CURRICULUM OF ALL ELEMENTARY AND SECONDARY SCHOOLS
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE In today’s hyperconnected world, the internet has become both a gateway to opportunity and a source of risk. The Philippines, with 90.8 million social media users as of January 2025—representing 78% of the population and averaging 3 hours and 32 minutes daily online use (DataReportal, We Are Social, Meltwater – Digital 2025 Report), ranks among the most active nations globally. This level of engagement underscores the urgent need for structured education on internet safety and media literacy. While young Filipinos are often described as “digital natives,” technical proficiency alone does not equate to digital literacy. Exposure to cyberbullying, misinformation, predatory grooming, and privacy breaches continues to rise, threatening both individual well-being and national resilience. This measure seeks to institutionalize an Internet Safety Education Program (ISEP) in all elementary and secondary schools. The program will equip teachers with professional training, empower students through peer-driven initiatives, and engage parents and communities in building a “360-degree” safety net. By embedding internet safety and media literacy into the curriculum, the bill ensures that the next generation is not only connected, but protected, informed, and responsible. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. ATTY. title: AN ACT PROTECTING SENIOR CITIZENS FROM VARIOUS FORMS OF FRAUD THROUGH INFORMATION DISSEMINATION AND PROVIDING MECHANISMS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE Senior citizens are increasingly vulnerable to fraud schemes that exploit mail, telecommunication, and online platforms. Common tactics such as phishing, text scams, and investment fraud not only cause financial losses but also bring emotional distress to the elderly. According to the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (2021 Financial Inclusion Survey), only 2% of respondents correctly answered all six basic financial literacy questions, showing limited awareness that makes seniors more prone to scams. The Anti-Money Laundering Council (2015 Strategic Analysis Report) further reported that cross-border investment fraud involving the Philippines amounted to ₱4.66 billion over five years, underscoring the scale of financial crimes that can affect vulnerable populations. This measure mandates the Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG), through local government units, to regularly disseminate information on mail, telemarketing, and internet fraud targeting senior citizens. It also requires coordination with agencies such as the BSP, SEC, NTC, DICT, and NBI to provide updated fraud prevention materials and reporting mechanisms. By institutionalizing education, awareness, and reporting systems, this bill ensures that senior citizens, their families, and caregivers are better equipped to recognize and avoid fraudulent schemes. It strengthens government accountability and affirms Congress’ commitment to safeguarding the welfare of the elderly in the digital age. In view of the foregoing, the immediate passage of this bill is earnestly sought. ATTY. title: AN ACT INSTITUTING THE MAGNA CARTA FOR CHILD DEVELOPMENT WORKERS AND PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR
explanatory_note: EXPLANATORY NOTE The early years of a child's life are critical to their physical, emotional, social, and cognitive development. During this period, Child Development Workers (CDWs) play a vital role in providing care, early education, protection, and developmental support to young children, particularly those in vulnerable and underserved communities. Despite the importance of their work, many CDWs continue to face challenges related to employment security, compensation, benefits, professional development, and access to adequate support and resources. These conditions may affect not only their welfare but also the quality and continuity of early childhood development services provided to children. CDWs perform responsibilities that require patience, dedication, specialized knowledge, and a deep commitment to the welfare of children. It is therefore necessary for the State to recognize their indispensable contribution to nation-building and ensure that they are provided with appropriate employment protection, fair compensation, benefits, training opportunities, and other forms of support. This measure seeks to establish a comprehensive framework for the protection and promotion of the rights and welfare of CDWs. It aims to strengthen their employment security, provide appropriate plantilla positions and compensation, promote continuing education and skills development, and ensure access to benefits and other privileges commensurate with the importance of their duties. By investing in the welfare and professional development of CDWs, the State likewise invests in the future of Filipino children. A well-supported and adequately protected workforce is essential to ensuring that every child receives quality care, early learning, and developmental support during the most formative years of life. In view of the foregoing, the passage of this bill is earnestly sought. ATTY.
